calls.title: The power play delivered
calls.plain: The Stars’ power play created at least its usual chances. Dallas went 3 for 5 on the power play.
calls.said: the Stars’ power play would get its usual chances against the Sharks’ shaky kill
calls.beyond: Dallas has one of the league’s most dangerous power plays, and San Jose has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: Dallas’s power play created 18.3 expected goals per 60, against their usual 9.7 (about 10.7 against San Jose) and a league average of 7.8. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

calls.head: Expect the Stars to have the puck more
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Stars have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Sharks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Stars’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

story.head: Harley has a goal and two assists as the Stars get past the Sharks
paras: The first period was a wild one. Michael Misa opened the scoring for the Sharks early in the period, but Roope Hintz tied it 1-1 for Dallas on the power play just under two minutes later. Jamie Benn and Jason Robertson scored a minute and a half apart late in the period to put the Stars up 3-1. Ivar Stenberg pulled the Sharks within one early in the second, with Eric Pohlkamp picking up his first NHL point on the goal. Thomas Harley extended the lead to 4-2 on the power play midway through the period, and that one stood up as the winner. Will Smith pulled the Sharks within one on the power play two and a half minutes later. The Sharks went more than 19 minutes without a shot on goal, from late in the second to late in the third, even with a power play in that stretch. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season. Two players had three-point nights: Harley with a goal and two assists, and the Sharks’ Macklin Celebrini with three assists.

The Stars carried the play, outshooting the Sharks 30-23, and got the result to match. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves for the Stars, and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 26 of 30 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Wyatt Johnston had the best night of anyone.

The Stars scored three power-play goals on five chances. A scrum at the end of the second sent four players to the box. The officials called 17 penalties, a total the league sees about once every 160 games. The Stars moved to 10-5-2 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Sharks fell to 7-11-1, sixth in the Pacific.
